text.p: RIGA, Jan 13 (Reuter) These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two robbers stole 135,800 lats from a post office car on Saturday after killing two and wounding one post office official.
- Former president of the Lettika bank, Valery Berlin, was injured on Friday in a bomb attack in Riga.
- Democratic party Saimnieks has approved the list of candidates to run for municipal elections in Riga. Ziedonis Chevers, head of the party, said he was convinced of Saimnieks election victory.

- Chevers will meet Prime Minister Andris Shkele to discuss the rejection by Shkele of the candidature of Sarmite Jegere to the post of finance minister and the criteria a candidate should meet. No new candidates have been named by the party.

- The Latvian Social Democratic Party during its eigth congress merged with the Taisniba (Justice) party. The two have decided on a further merger with the Latvian Social Democratic Labour Party by the end of 1997.
- Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjorn Tore Godal arrives in Latvia today to discuss bilateral relations.
- Latvenergo, the state-owned electricity company, hopes to receive compensation from the Balta insurance company for the damage caused by the heavy snow falls during the last three weeks.
- Shkele refused to comment to the press on his five-hour private visit to Lithuania. He met Lithuanian counterpart Gediminas Vagnorius and parliament speaker Vytautas Landsbergis.
- Tax collection has improved, with revenues from VAT up by 21.7 percent during 1996. Revenues from excise tax have also risen sharply, showing almost a 2.5-fold increase.
- The Privatisation Agency has allowed the debts of 18 state-owned enterprises worth around five million lats to be capitalised.
- GEC Alsthom will install generating equipment to modernise a hydroelectric power station on the Daugava River, some 50 kms to the east of Riga.
